top.title: How Vanessa DiBernardo, 'Mom-V-P', helped Current win NWSL Championship after pregnancy
top.description: WASHINGTON — Vanessa DiBernardo began the 2026 season pregnant. She ended it on Saturday with a baby in her right arm and an NWSL trophy in her left, with streamers strewn across Audi Field and with her Kansas City Current teammates chanting: “Mom-V-P! Mom-V-P!” In between, there were all sorts of unexpected challenges and emotions that only moms can really understand. “The first 30 to 60 days of motherhood is a wild ride,” DiBernardo said with a laugh. But after giving birth to her daughter, Charlie Mae, in January, she slowly worked her way back to professional soccer. And on Saturday, at 34 years old, in her 13th year as an NWSL player, DiBernardo won her first championship. She won it with an Olimpico, a goal directly from a corner, in the 54th minute of a dramatic 2-1 victory over the Washington Spirit . “That’s the brilliance you need in finals, in playoffs,” midfielder and captain Lo’eau LaBonta said. top.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
top.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings Verstappen in control despite lead changes "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. top.title: Why Raiders owner Mark Davis called Christian Bale’s ‘unfair’ portrayal of father Al Davis a ‘crime’
top.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images ‘Madden,’ the biopic chronicling the life of John Madden, has upset Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis for the way his father, Al Davis, was made to look in the new movie. The movie was released on Amazon Prime earlier this week and shows the impact the legendary head coach and announcer had on the sport. One of his closest allies was Al Davis, who once served as the coach of the Raiders before becoming the general manager and principal owner, and who plays a key role in the movie. Mark Davis goes off on ‘Madden’ portraying his father negatively over Darryl Stingley incident Speaking in an interview with USA Today Sports , Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis spoke about the portrayal of his father, Al Davis, in ‘Madden,’ the recent biopic about John Madden. He admitted that he was hurt by the way his father’s involvement in John Madden’s dealings with Darryl Stingley was portrayed, suggesting that it was not fair to make him look like a bad person. “I did the best I could to protect him,” Davis told USA Today. “It’s absolutely a crime that they’re able to treat people that have passed away and characterise them in ways that are unfair, and there’s nobody around to protect their legacies. It’s just unfair. I don’t know what the purpose of the movie was, to be real honest. “I don’t blame Christian Bale. I don’t blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do. “For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him… That was just such a hurt to me personally because that’s my father’s legacy is how he treated people. “No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That’s one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way.” In the scene he is referencing, Al Davis is trying to convince John Madden not to visit Darryl Stingley at the hospital after the WR suffered a paralysing injury in a preseason game. While Mark Davis didn’t deny the veracity of the incident, he did feel that this one scene did damage to his father’s reputation in the long run. top.title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
top.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos. Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order. “I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said. His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu. Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis. “In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation. He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.” Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add. “Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time. He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative. Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis. “I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. top.title: Winners and losers from F1's chaotically extraordinary Las Vegas GP
top.description: Motorsport photo A pack of cars covered by seconds, the top three trading first position as part of 35 lead changes, and drivers trying to figure out the best positioning to be ahead at the finish line on the final lap; The Las Vegas Grand Prix felt like the glitzy, battery-assisted street course version of the Indy 500. It was quite fitting to see how in America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put on an entertaining, if somewhat artificial, spectacle. It may not have been everyone's cup of tea, but you'll be hard-pressed to find anyone in attendance that didn't feel like they got their hard-earned money's worth. Winner: Max Verstappen What did it take to triumph on the Las Vegas Strip? Guts and racecraft, sure. But also brainpower. Figuring out the right energy deployment strategy to stay at the front, and then tweaking that strategy to be ahead crossing the line on the final lap rather than into Turn 1. Verstappen provided some insight into his thinking on that very subject through his communication with Red Bull. "You guys have to look at the deployment of the final lap because they’ve figured it out. They can stay ahead of me until the line, so we need to see what we need to do for the final lap only." In the end, his plan worked as he held off Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri . But not before mocking George Russell's unsuccessful move on Kimi Antonelli, a day after he clashed with the Mercedes driver in qualifying. top.title: Wisconsin 3, Penn State 2: Groundhog Day
top.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 13: Joshua Fleming #34 of the Penn State Nittany Lions watches the play during the first period against the Michigan Wolverines at Yost Ice Arena on November 13, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images To cap a weekend Penn State athletics would love to forget, the men’s hockey team fell 3-2 to No. 2 Wisconsin on Saturday night. It was another tough effort for the struggling Nittany Lions, but the Badgers scored the game-winning goal with four seconds left in regulation to secure a sweep over Penn State. How It Happened Vasily Zelenov scored early in the first period to give Wisconsin a 1-0 lead. He got behind the Penn State defense and was just able to tuck the puck home on the backhand past Ryder Fetterolf. Justin Poirier tied the game with his second goal of the weekend later in the first on the power play. Dane Dowiak found him wide open and fed him a perfect cross-ice pass to give Poirier a high-danger chance on the one-timer. Late in the first period, JJ Wiebusch was left all alone in front of the net, and the junior scored against his former team to give Wisconsin the lead back at 2-1. A scoreless second period helped Penn State hang around in a game they were throughly outplayed. Ryder Fetterolf kept the Lions in the game with several huge saves. Luke Misa eventually tied the game in the third period for Penn State. Jackson Smith found him open at the doorstep and slid a perfect pass to him for an easy goal. It appeared Penn State would at least get a point for their effort, but Oliver Tulk slipped the game-winning goal past Ryder Fetterolf with four seconds left in regulation. Wisconsin had a good set play for the final sequence and won a huge offensive zone faceoff with 10 seconds left to set up the game-winning goal. Penn State fell to 2-11-1 with yet another heartbreaking loss. Random Observations Numbness- I am running out of unique ways to see Penn State athletics lose games. With football’s loss to Rutgers, the women’s soccer team getting upset by Villanova in the NCAA tournament in OT, and now this, these losses are all starting to blend together. Outplayed- The game was close on the scoreboard, but Wisconsin outshot Penn State 48-25. Goaltending kept the game within reach, but the Nittany Lions were not consistent on offense and gave up far too many good looks to Wisconsin. Ryder Fetterolf- The freshman goalie has been up and down this season, but last night was one of his best performances. What a shame they couldn’t at least get a point from another strong goaltending night. What’s Next Penn State will host Princeton on Friday. Puck drop is scheduled for 5pm on Big Ten Plus.

top.title: ‘If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here’ – Bruno Fernandes discusses his Man Utd future
top.description: ‘If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here’ – Bruno Fernandes discusses his Man Utd future Bruno Fernandes has confirmed Manchester United have offered him a new contract but says he has put discussions on hold while the club focuses on returning to winning ways. The United captain’s current deal expires at the end of the season, although the club hold an option to extend it by a further year. Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United, according to Sky Sports News, but dismissed suggestions that he is demanding more money or a longer deal. “No, there’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years,” Fernandes told Sky Sports . “If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. “I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.” The 32-year-old insisted he has repeatedly chosen to remain at Old Trafford despite opportunities to leave. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here,” he said. “The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.” Fernandes also made clear he would not stand in United’s way if the club decided it was time for him to leave. “In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door,” he said. top.title: Bruno Fernandes admits Man United offered him new contract but ‘not the right moment’ for negotiations
top.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed that discussions over a new contract have stalled because it isn’t “the right moment” to be negotiating. The Portuguese said an offer had been made in the summer, with his contract due to expire at the end of this season, but negotiations were not ongoing as he insisted on prioritising the club’s return to form. The 32-year-old, who most recently signed in August 2024, has repeatedly been linked with a move away from Old Trafford . United have an option to trigger and extension for a further year. Fernandes told Sky Sports : “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. “We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.” United sit 19th in the Premier League after a dismal start to this campaign and parted ways with manager Michael Carrick after just 10 games, with former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino taking the reins. The Argentine’s first game in charge will be United’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday in their first game back after the international window. Fernandes stressed his loyalty to the club and added that he would not run down his contract if United decided it was in their interests for him to leave. He said: “No, there's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. “I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it's time to part ways’, I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.”

top.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following home win over lowly Bucks
top.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers were able to escape on Saturday with a 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks as they caught some fortunate breaks. The officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds before being fouled late and they also ruled Tyler Herro's game-tying shot was late as the Sixers improved to 12-0 in clutch games and 14-3 on the season overall. LeBron James finished with 21 points, six rebounds, and six assists. Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds, and nine assists while Anfernee Simons had 18 points off the bench. Tyrese Maxey had 17 points, four rebounds, and four assists, and VJ Edgecombe had 16 points and six assists. Jabari Walker poured in nine points, seven rebounds, and four assists and Dominick Barlow had 12 points in his season debut. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had 11 points. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win: 12-0 in clutch games Is there work to do? Absolutely. But everybody and the Sixers knew that. This isn't new. The ending of this game was sloppy and it almost cost them as the young Bucks looked desperate to end a lengthy 12-game losing streak. James and Co. know they have to be better as they move forward, but there is no questioning this team's resolve and ability to just win these types of games. It's certainly better to acknowledge that there's work to do after another win rather than a loss. "I mean, it's good to build that part of our game," said James. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're gonna play as hard as they can for their minutes. It's about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn't do well tonight, and that's gonna be good for the long term." Embiid continues to move better A tell-tale sign of Embiid getting back into shape is him grabbing a ton of rebounds. That takes energy and sometimes requires a second jump. Embiid was able to come up with some big rebounds against Bucks big men Myles Turner and Kel’el Ware and give the Sixers a big boost in that area of the game. When he is able to grab rebounds and make plays for his teammates, that fuels his overall game and the Sixers benefited from that against Milwaukee on Saturday. It also helps that he was able to put the ball in the basket as well. "He's obviously much more involved, and I think playing more assertively," said coach Nick Nurse. "I like the number of in-the-paint, at-the-rim, those kinds of attempts that he's taking. I think that's always a good sign. He looks like he's got his rhythm and confidence back on the offensive end. I’m really happy with the rebounds, to be honest with you, I think his defensive rebounding is great. Rebounding and defensive rebounding's been great." Barlow’s return The season debut could not have gone better for Barlow. He was super efficient, active on the defensive end, and provided some more size and athleticism at the big man spot that the Sixers have been missing throughout

According to police, the driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and hit another vehicle before crashing into a utility pole. Harrell was thrown forward into the windscreen and lost consciousness. The rideshare driver sustained minor injuries and was treated at the scene, while the driver of the second vehicle was uninjured. Tennessee Titans said in a statement they are in "constant communication" with Harrell's family and are working to gather further information. "At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care," the Titans added. "We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. Nelly Korda admits being uncomfortable despite a stunning 65 at the CME Group Tour Championship It is remarkable to think that Korda has not won on the LPGA Tour since clinching the US Women’s Open at Riviera back in June. At that stage, there was even talk about whether she would have any chance of completing the Career Grand Slam in 2026. Korda failed to capitalise after an opening 63 at The ANNIKA earlier this month. And she has only had one top-five finish since her most recent major triumph in the Pacific Palisades. But Saturday may have been a turning point. And after the round, Korda explained what changed for her. “I found something for sure. I mean, I still left maybe a couple shots out right, very like uncharacteristic out right,” she said. “But overall, really happy with what I found on range. It was more of like a takeaway thought versus an actual position thought. top.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts’ decision to release Daniel Jones after sticking with him for most of the season has come under fresh scrutiny after ESPN insider Stephen Holder highlighted several details he believes have been overlooked. Stephen Holder offers fresh perspective on Indianapolis Colts’ Daniel Jones decision Taking to X, Holder acknowledged that Indianapolis could potentially have traded Jones before the deadline for a minimal return, but argued that several factors need to be considered. He first pointed out that the Colts had played only two games since the trade deadline, with both being arguably Jones’ worst performances of the season. Holder also questioned why a quarterback change had not happened earlier, while suggesting head coach Shane Steichen had been allowed to continue with Jones by ownership. He wrote : “Should they have made a QB change earlier? Obviously. But ownership was allowing Shane Steichen to stick w his QB. I’m personally not a fan of owners dictating who plays but maybe that’s just me.” The ESPN insider also discussed the lack of convincing trade interest, claiming Minnesota appeared focused on Kirk Cousins while Baltimore had only offered “something” that was not particularly substantial. Another overlooked factor was Jones’ contract situation. He was still under contract for 2027, meaning there was a possibility he could have improved with more time removed from his injury. Holder was careful to acknowledge that this was a significant projection and could prove completely wrong. Indianapolis are now left to move forward with Richardson under centre as they attempt to recover from a difficult run of results. top.description: “I didn’t know about it” Mudryk reveals how his Arsenal dream was killed by agent Arsenal made a major effort to sign Mykhailo Mudryk during the January 2023 transfer window , when the winger was establishing himself as one of the most exciting attacking talents in European football. The Gunners had monitored his development for an extended period and were determined to bring him to the Emirates as soon as Shakhtar Donetsk became willing to sell. For much of the negotiations, Arsenal appeared to be in a strong position to secure his signature. The club continued working towards an agreement, seemingly doing everything possible to win the race for a player who was keen to represent them. However, the situation changed as the transfer window progressed, and their hopes of completing the deal began to fade. Chelsea moved ahead in the transfer race Towards the end of the negotiations, Mudryk’s representatives appeared to pay less attention to Arsenal’s interest, while discussions no longer seemed to be progressing as positively as they had earlier. It eventually emerged that Shakhtar Donetsk and the player’s entourage favoured a move to Chelsea. The Blues were prepared to offer significantly more in transfer fees and commissions, giving them an advantage in the negotiations. Arsenal consequently missed out on a player they had pursued for some time, with Mudryk completing his move to Stamford Bridge instead of joining the club he had reportedly wanted to represent. The transfer meant that the winger had to put aside his ambition of playing for Arsenal, something he has now discussed publicly. His latest comments have provided an insight into what happened behind the scenes and how his preferred destination differed from the club he eventually joined. Mudryk explains his disappointment The attacker has now opened up about his desire to play for Arsenal and his understanding of the negotiations involving his representatives. He said via Fabrizio Romano : “Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret. “Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates was my dream. “There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal. nigeria.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. nigeria.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
nigeria.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. sports.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. sports.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images ‘Madden,’ the biopic chronicling the life of John Madden, has upset Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis for the way his father, Al Davis, was made to look in the new movie. The movie was released on Amazon Prime earlier this week and shows the impact the legendary head coach and announcer had on the sport. One of his closest allies was Al Davis, who once served as the coach of the Raiders before becoming the general manager and principal owner, and who plays a key role in the movie. Mark Davis goes off on ‘Madden’ portraying his father negatively over Darryl Stingley incident Speaking in an interview with USA Today Sports , Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis spoke about the portrayal of his father, Al Davis, in ‘Madden,’ the recent biopic about John Madden. He admitted that he was hurt by the way his father’s involvement in John Madden’s dealings with Darryl Stingley was portrayed, suggesting that it was not fair to make him look like a bad person. “I did the best I could to protect him,” Davis told USA Today. “It’s absolutely a crime that they’re able to treat people that have passed away and characterise them in ways that are unfair, and there’s nobody around to protect their legacies. It’s just unfair. I don’t know what the purpose of the movie was, to be real honest. “I don’t blame Christian Bale. I don’t blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do. “For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him… That was just such a hurt to me personally because that’s my father’s legacy is how he treated people. “No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That’s one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way.” In the scene he is referencing, Al Davis is trying to convince John Madden not to visit Darryl Stingley at the hospital after the WR suffered a paralysing injury in a preseason game. It was quite fitting to see how in America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put on an entertaining, if somewhat artificial, spectacle. It may not have been everyone's cup of tea, but you'll be hard-pressed to find anyone in attendance that didn't feel like they got their hard-earned money's worth. Winner: Max Verstappen What did it take to triumph on the Las Vegas Strip? Guts and racecraft, sure. But also brainpower. Figuring out the right energy deployment strategy to stay at the front, and then tweaking that strategy to be ahead crossing the line on the final lap rather than into Turn 1. Verstappen provided some insight into his thinking on that very subject through his communication with Red Bull. "You guys have to look at the deployment of the final lap because they’ve figured it out. They can stay ahead of me until the line, so we need to see what we need to do for the final lap only." In the end, his plan worked as he held off Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri . But not before mocking George Russell's unsuccessful move on Kimi Antonelli, a day after he clashed with the Mercedes driver in qualifying. sports.title: Wisconsin 3, Penn State 2: Groundhog Day
sports.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 13: Joshua Fleming #34 of the Penn State Nittany Lions watches the play during the first period against the Michigan Wolverines at Yost Ice Arena on November 13, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images To cap a weekend Penn State athletics would love to forget, the men’s hockey team fell 3-2 to No. 2 Wisconsin on Saturday night. It was another tough effort for the struggling Nittany Lions, but the Badgers scored the game-winning goal with four seconds left in regulation to secure a sweep over Penn State. How It Happened Vasily Zelenov scored early in the first period to give Wisconsin a 1-0 lead. He got behind the Penn State defense and was just able to tuck the puck home on the backhand past Ryder Fetterolf. Justin Poirier tied the game with his second goal of the weekend later in the first on the power play. Dane Dowiak found him wide open and fed him a perfect cross-ice pass to give Poirier a high-danger chance on the one-timer. Late in the first period, JJ Wiebusch was left all alone in front of the net, and the junior scored against his former team to give Wisconsin the lead back at 2-1. A scoreless second period helped Penn State hang around in a game they were throughly outplayed. Ryder Fetterolf kept the Lions in the game with several huge saves. Luke Misa eventually tied the game in the third period for Penn State. Jackson Smith found him open at the doorstep and slid a perfect pass to him for an easy goal. It appeared Penn State would at least get a point for their effort, but Oliver Tulk slipped the game-winning goal past Ryder Fetterolf with four seconds left in regulation. Wisconsin had a good set play for the final sequence and won a huge offensive zone faceoff with 10 seconds left to set up the game-winning goal. Penn State fell to 2-11-1 with yet another heartbreaking loss. Random Observations Numbness- I am running out of unique ways to see Penn State athletics lose games. With football’s loss to Rutgers, the women’s soccer team getting upset by Villanova in the NCAA tournament in OT, and now this, these losses are all starting to blend together. Outplayed- The game was close on the scoreboard, but Wisconsin outshot Penn State 48-25. Goaltending kept the game within reach, but the Nittany Lions were not consistent on offense and gave up far too many good looks to Wisconsin. Ryder Fetterolf- The freshman goalie has been up and down this season, but last night was one of his best performances. What a shame they couldn’t at least get a point from another strong goaltending night. What’s Next Penn State will host Princeton on Friday. Puck drop is scheduled for 5pm on Big Ten Plus.

sports.description: ‘If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here’ – Bruno Fernandes discusses his Man Utd future Bruno Fernandes has confirmed Manchester United have offered him a new contract but says he has put discussions on hold while the club focuses on returning to winning ways. The United captain’s current deal expires at the end of the season, although the club hold an option to extend it by a further year. Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United, according to Sky Sports News, but dismissed suggestions that he is demanding more money or a longer deal. “No, there’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years,” Fernandes told Sky Sports . “If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. “I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.” The 32-year-old insisted he has repeatedly chosen to remain at Old Trafford despite opportunities to leave. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here,” he said. “The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.” Fernandes also made clear he would not stand in United’s way if the club decided it was time for him to leave. “In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door,” he said. sports.title: Bruno Fernandes admits Man United offered him new contract but ‘not the right moment’ for negotiations
sports.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed that discussions over a new contract have stalled because it isn’t “the right moment” to be negotiating. The Portuguese said an offer had been made in the summer, with his contract due to expire at the end of this season, but negotiations were not ongoing as he insisted on prioritising the club’s return to form. The 32-year-old, who most recently signed in August 2024, has repeatedly been linked with a move away from Old Trafford . United have an option to trigger and extension for a further year. Fernandes told Sky Sports : “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. “We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.” United sit 19th in the Premier League after a dismal start to this campaign and parted ways with manager Michael Carrick after just 10 games, with former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino taking the reins. The Argentine’s first game in charge will be United’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday in their first game back after the international window. Fernandes stressed his loyalty to the club and added that he would not run down his contract if United decided it was in their interests for him to leave. He said: “No, there's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. “I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it's time to part ways’, I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.”

sports.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers were able to escape on Saturday with a 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks as they caught some fortunate breaks. The officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds before being fouled late and they also ruled Tyler Herro's game-tying shot was late as the Sixers improved to 12-0 in clutch games and 14-3 on the season overall. LeBron James finished with 21 points, six rebounds, and six assists. Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds, and nine assists while Anfernee Simons had 18 points off the bench. Tyrese Maxey had 17 points, four rebounds, and four assists, and VJ Edgecombe had 16 points and six assists. Jabari Walker poured in nine points, seven rebounds, and four assists and Dominick Barlow had 12 points in his season debut. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had 11 points. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win: 12-0 in clutch games Is there work to do? Absolutely. But everybody and the Sixers knew that. This isn't new. The ending of this game was sloppy and it almost cost them as the young Bucks looked desperate to end a lengthy 12-game losing streak. James and Co. know they have to be better as they move forward, but there is no questioning this team's resolve and ability to just win these types of games. It's certainly better to acknowledge that there's work to do after another win rather than a loss. "I mean, it's good to build that part of our game," said James. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're gonna play as hard as they can for their minutes. Embiid was able to come up with some big rebounds against Bucks big men Myles Turner and Kel’el Ware and give the Sixers a big boost in that area of the game. When he is able to grab rebounds and make plays for his teammates, that fuels his overall game and the Sixers benefited from that against Milwaukee on Saturday. It also helps that he was able to put the ball in the basket as well. "He's obviously much more involved, and I think playing more assertively," said coach Nick Nurse. "I like the number of in-the-paint, at-the-rim, those kinds of attempts that he's taking. I think that's always a good sign. He looks like he's got his rhythm and confidence back on the offensive end. I’m really happy with the rebounds, to be honest with you, I think his defensive rebounding is great. Rebounding and defensive rebounding's been great." Barlow’s return The season debut could not have gone better for Barlow. sports.title: Enzo Maresca has sent a message to his Manchester City squad ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League meeting with Napoli, following Saturday's draw with Fulham.
sports.description: Enzo Maresca has sent a message to his Manchester City squad ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League meeting with Napoli, following Saturday's draw with Fulham. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? Maresca watched his side fall behind to Rodrigo Muniz's 16th-minute strike at the Etihad Stadium, before Elliot Anderson levelled with a drilled volley from the edge of the area in the 57th minute after a Phil Foden corner was cleared, scoring his second goal for the club since his summer move from Nottingham Forest . Manchester City also had a first-half goal from Erling Haaland ruled out, with the Premier League explaining the decision by stating that Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was deemed to have had control of the ball. The point ended a run of three successive league defeats to Aston Villa , Brighton and Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest , but it extended City's winless run in the Premier League to four matches. Maresca's side enjoyed 60 percent of possession against Marco Silva and co and 14 shots against Fulham, but only managed two on target, and they sit third in the table, level on points with Brighton and five behind leaders Arsenal , though the Seagulls can go three points clear of Manchester City by beating Hull City at the MKM Stadium on Sunday. Maresca: It's a massive game on Tuesday, hopefully we can win Speaking to TNT Sports after the game, Maresca reflected on the chances his side created in Saturday's frustrating draw against Fulham and looked ahead to Napoli. "We had so many moments that we could have made some better choices," the Italian said. "But again, it's important that we arrive there, we create chances, and hopefully soon we can score more goals and win. "We need to do many things better [vs Napoli]. It's a massive game on Tuesday and hopefully, we can win." The Italian then explained the tactical changes he made at the interval, with Manchester City having failed to thwart wave after wave of Fulham attacks in the opening 45 minutes. Maresca added: "We changed a little at half-time, also the way we were pressing. We prepared the pressing one way, they changed something, so at half-time we changed. [In the] second-half, we were much better. Again, it's also part of something when you are building." Anderson's equaliser arrived 12 minutes after the restart and Maresca introduced all of Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Josko Gvardiol and Allan Elias to push for a winner that never came as the Blues failed to win for a fourth Premier League game. The only thing we can do is just try to recover, says Maresca as Man City drop further points Maresca also addressed his side's habit of conceding early, with Manchester City once again conceding early courtesy of deep-lying issues in defence and midfield. "Again, we are conceding many goals, especially in the beginning of the game," the 46-year-old said. "But at the end, we create chances, we score goals, we need to try to find a way to keep clean sheets and win games.

technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.
